title: NetSuite HubSpot Integration: Unify Sales and Finance Data
summary: NetSuite HubSpot integration connects your CRM and ERP to automate lead-to-cash workflows and eliminate manual data entry between platforms.
body_markdown:
## Syncing HubSpot contacts to NetSuite


Moving data from a front-office engagement signal to a back-office financial record requires a structured sequence. By treating the integration as a series of distinct logic gates, you'll avoid the common pitfall of flooding the ERP with unqualified leads that haven't yet met billing requirements.


### Stage 1: Set the HubSpot 'Contact Updated' trigger


Monitoring the[HubSpot](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces/hubspot) "New or Updated Contact" trigger allows the integration to capture any profile changes that occur during the sales cycle.


You'll prefer this specific trigger over "New Contact" because financial data, such as a Tax ID or billing address, rarely exists at the moment of initial lead creation. The workflow remains dormant until the salesperson populates the specific properties required for a successful NetSuite record.


### Filtering leads by lifecycle stage before sync


Every marketing lead would consume a seat in the ERP if data did not pass a filter step checking if the` lifecycle_stage` property equals "Customer." Revenue Operations teams found that without this gate, the NetSuite sandbox became cluttered with junk data within a single week.


Only records with high intent and verified data move forward to the accounting layer once you implement this strict condition.


### Stage 3: Authenticate the NetSuite 'Custom API Call' action


The workflow initiates a[NetSuite](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces/netsuite) "Custom API Call" action to post the data to a RESTlet or the standard REST API once the filter passes.


Because the standard catalog often lacks the specific custom segments used by finance for regional reporting, the custom call includes specific headers and internal IDs. Token-Based Authentication (TBA) is required at this stage.


TBA creates a secure connection that doesn't expire when an administrator changes their password.


### Mapping HubSpot email and company fields to NetSuite


To ensure record uniqueness, the mapping layer translates the HubSpot` email` and` company` fields into the corresponding NetSuite` email` and` companyName` keys. To handle edge cases where a company name might be missing, a "Branch" step or a fallback value should be used.


The following table illustrates the essential mapping requirements for a standard B2B sync:


HubSpot Property NetSuite Field Purpose


Email email Primary key for duplicate detection


Company Name companyName Legal entity name for invoicing


HubSpot Contact ID externalId Links the two records for future updates


These steps are visualized in the screenshot of the workflow builder. It specifically highlights how a "Contact Updated" trigger flows through an "AI Agent" step for qualification before reaching the NetSuite Customer action.


This visual logic allows your program lead to verify the "Qualified?" condition position before any data reaches the ERP.


### Stage 5: Run a manual test to verify record creation


Confirming that the NetSuite Internal ID is returned and logged back in HubSpot requires a manual execution using a test contact. Successfully receiving an HTTP 201 Created response means the field types are compatible and the permissions are correctly scoped.


The workflow can be toggled to an active state once your team verifies this handshake. This allows the automated sync to take over the manual entry tasks previously handled by the accounting team.
